paper_metadata.title: Effect of Zr addition on the stability of precipitated Laves phase and mechanical properties of Fe–Cr–Al-based alloys at high temperatures
paper_metadata.journal: Progress in Natural Science: Materials International

evidence.quote: The effect of a small amount of Zr addition on the temperature-dependent stability of Laves phase particles and mechanical properties of Fe-13.5Cr-4.73Al-2.07Mo-(0.34–0.5)Nb-(0.65–0.98)Ta-(0–0.33)Zr (wt. %) ferritic alloys was investigated in the present study.
the alloy without Zr is designated as F0–0Zr
the Zr-containing alloys are designated as F1-0.1Zr (0.11 wt. % Zr)

other.raw_purity: Fe, Al, Zr 99.99 wt.%; Mo, Nb, Ta 99.5 wt.%; Cr 99.9 wt.%

evidence.quote: Alloy ingots with about 100 g for each were prepared by vacuum arc-melting, in which the purities of the raw metals are 99.99 wt. % for Fe, Al, Zr, 99.5 wt. % for Mo, Nb, Ta, and 99.9 wt. % for Cr, respectively.
These ingots were homogenized (i.e., solid-solutionized) at 1473 K for 2 h
hot-rolled at 1073 K for several times with a total deformation of about 90%.
Then these hot-rolled plates with a thickness of about 1.5 mm were aged at 1073 K for 24 h.

Finally, the aged plate samples were re-treated at 1273 K, 1323 K, 1373 K, and 1473 K for 1 h, respectively, to investigate the thermal stability of microstructures (especially the precipitated particles) at HTs. Each heat treatment was followed by a water-quenching cooling.

the gray particles (marked with red circles) were enriched by the Zr element alone, with an average composition of Fe62.13Cr6.25Al11.36Mo1.21Nb0.91Ta2.45Zr15.78 (at. %), in which the ratio of Fe to Zr was close to 23:6, determined as the Fe23Zr6 phase.

the bright precipitated particles were still dominant in the 1273 K-treated alloys, with a volume fraction of about 2.0% and a particle size of about 300–450 nm
